title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 41 (Effect of accepting performance from third person)

content.overview: Section 41 provides that when a promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, he cannot afterwards enforce it against the promisor.
content.glance: Acceptance of performance from a third person discharges the original promisor as against the promisee.
content.study: If the promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, the promisee cannot afterwards enforce that promise against the original promisor. Mere offer by a third person without acceptance does not discharge. Current-law framing: identify performance by a third person; test acceptance by the promisee; conclude that the promisor cannot be enforced against for the same promise.

sections.heading: Acceptance from third person
sections.body: When the promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, he cannot afterwards enforce it against the promisor.

provisions.title: Effect of accepting performance from third person

examples.title: Third-party payment accepted
examples.body: A owes B ₹10,000. C pays B and B accepts. B cannot afterwards enforce the same debt against A under s. 41.

hypotheticals.question: Does a third person’s offer without acceptance discharge the promisor?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 41 requires acceptance of performance by the promisee.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-41
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Any third-party attempt to perform automatically discharges the promisor.
misconceptions.correction: Only acceptance of that performance by the promisee triggers s. 41.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 41 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify performance by a third person. II. Test acceptance by the promisee. III. Conclude promisor cannot be enforced against. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Stress acceptance as the key trigger.
